sources.kind: Systematic reviews of cohorts and randomised trials
sources.limitations: Original abstract read. Disease endpoints largely observational; chronic-disease populations and supplement trials excluded. Linked erratum identified; numerical estimates withheld pending full-text/erratum appraisal.

sources.limitations: Original abstract read; component estimates depend on modelling assumptions and undetected interactions. Do not prescribe individual treatment components.

sources.title: Effect of breathwork on stress and mental health: A meta-analysis of randomised-controlled trials
sources.limitations: Original abstract read; small studies, moderate bias concerns, heterogeneous methods and self-report. Searches through February 2022.

sources.title: Effect of coherent breathing on mental health and wellbeing: a randomised placebo-controlled trial
sources.limitations: Original abstract read. One tested breathing protocol, online adult sample and short follow-up; no detectable superiority does not prove all breathing methods ineffective.

sources.title: Effects of mindfulness-based interventions on perceived stress among non-clinical adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.limitations: Original abstract read. Searches through August 2025; perceived stress rather than disease endpoints; programmes and controls differ.

sources.title: Diet, physical activity or both for prevention or delay of type 2 diabetes mellitus and its associated complications in people at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus
sources.limitations: Summary and detailed abstract read; searches/alerts through 2017. High-risk populations, mostly impaired glucose tolerance. Not evidence for the app or proof of synergy.

sources.title: Effects of exercise on sleep quality in general population: Meta-analysis and systematic review
sources.limitations: Original abstract read; published online November 2024. Different exercise and sleep measures; reported moderator statistics need full-text verification; no numerical ranking reproduced.

sources.title: Effect of Sleep Extension on Objectively Assessed Energy Intake Among Adults With Overweight in Real-life Settings: A Randomized Clinical Trial
sources.limitations: Original abstract read; 80 younger adults with overweight and habitual short sleep; short intervention. Not a general weight-loss recommendation.

sources.title: The behaviour change wheel: A new method for characterising and designing behaviour change interventions
sources.limitations: Framework design evidence, not a trial showing this planner changes health outcomes.

sources.title: Mental health of adolescents
sources.limitations: Adolescent context; supportive families/schools and access to care, not adult self-treatment instructions.

sources.title: Behaviour change: individual approaches
sources.limitations: 403 on original page and PDF; NOT VERIFIED in this assessment. Cannot support a lesson pending access.

claims.scientificClaim: UK guidance for ages 19–64 recommends at least 150 moderate or 75 vigorous aerobic minutes weekly, plus strengthening on at least two days.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Population recommendation; not a biological cutoff.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults aged 19–64.

claims.scientificClaim: Moderate activity usually permits conversation but not singing; vigorous activity makes sustained conversation harder.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Practical intensity indicator, not a personal exercise safety test.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Repeated suitable aerobic activity supports cardiovascular capacity and everyday function.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Established guidance/physiology; effects vary by activity and person.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Greater and increasing activity are associated with lower mortality; benefits are not restricted to a single weekly threshold.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Large consistent cohorts; confounding and reverse causation prevent personal causal estimates.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Balance and functional exercise programmes reduce falls in community-dwelling older adults.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Cochrane grades falls outcomes high certainty; harms/fractures less certain.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Community-dwelling older adults; not every walking or resistance programme.

claims.scientificClaim: Older-adult activity guidance includes strength, balance and flexibility alongside aerobic activity.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Age-specific guidance; adapt to current fitness.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults 65 and over.

claims.scientificClaim: Physical activity includes walking, cycling, wheeling and activity in daily life; access and suitability vary.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Global guidance supports inclusive options, not universal exercise routines.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Balanced eating concerns variety and the pattern across meals; the Eatwell Guide need not be matched at every meal.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Public-health pattern guidance, not proof that a diagram itself prevents disease.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Starchy foods supply energy; protein foods, vegetables and dairy or suitable alternatives contribute different overlapping nutrients.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Established food composition and physiology; foods are not single-nutrient compartments.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Fibre supports bowel function; higher fibre intake is associated with better long-term outcomes and trials support some intermediate outcomes.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Disease outcomes largely observational; intermediate trial outcomes are not disease prevention proofs.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: UK adult fibre guidance is 30 g daily; this is not a universal target for every age or therapeutic diet.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Population guidance; individual dietary needs differ.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: General adult population; not children or prescribed modified diets.

claims.scientificClaim: Mediterranean-style dietary intervention evidence varies by outcome and comparison; universal cardiovascular guarantees are unjustified.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: Some outcomes favour intervention; other outcomes show little/no clear difference. Newer dietary trial appraisal remains outstanding.
claims.certaintyRationale: Older review with few clinical endpoint trials and heterogeneous interventions.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults in primary/secondary prevention research; not a treatment programme.

claims.scientificClaim: Frozen and tinned fruit or vegetables can contribute to balanced eating; a whole-food percentage cannot establish nutrient adequacy.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Guidance supports varied practical choices; no validated app percentage exists.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: European dietary reference values differ by population and are not an individual meal prescription.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Scientific reference overview rather than one pan-European diet.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Population groups differ in age and life stage.

claims.scientificClaim: Many adults need around 7–9 hours; duration and daytime functioning both matter.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: General adult range with individual variation; duration is not diagnostic.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: CDC recommends 8–10 hours for ages 13–17, at least 7 for ages 18–60, 7–9 for ages 61–64 and 7–8 for 65+.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Named age bands; do not average with another guideline.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Specified age bands only.

claims.scientificClaim: Sleep timing reflects daily biological clocks and accumulating sleep pressure; light provides timing cues.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Established basic sleep regulation; not a personal light-treatment protocol.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Multicomponent CBT-I improves insomnia outcomes and is different from general sleep tips.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Consistent trial syntheses; delivery, comparators and component assumptions vary.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults with assessed insomnia, including studied chronic conditions.

claims.scientificClaim: Shift workers need advice adapted to their actual sleep opportunity and circumstances.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Workplace advice supports flexibility, not one optimal schedule.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Shift workers and their households.

claims.scientificClaim: Persistent sleep problems affecting daily life warrant assessment; do not drive when sleepy.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Authoritative safety/help-seeking guidance; no diagnosis made.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Stress can affect alertness, tension, mood, sleep, appetite and behaviour; responses differ.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Established broad responses; symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose stress.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Gentle unforced breathing is an optional coping practice rather than a required technique.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Source-specific instructions; not evidence for forceful breathwork or breath holding.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Small trials suggest breathwork can reduce self-reported stress, but specific superiority over credible active comparisons is uncertain.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: Fincham 2023 active-comparator trial found no detectable superiority of coherent breathing; both groups improved.
claims.certaintyRationale: Small studies, bias concerns and heterogeneous controls; a larger active-comparator trial found no detectable added benefit.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Mindfulness programmes may reduce perceived stress; physiological and long-term disease effects are not established by that outcome.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Original abstract assessed; programmes/controls differ and full-text appraisal outstanding.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Non-clinical adults in included trials.

claims.scientificClaim: Practical support, social connection and addressing pressures belong alongside individual coping skills.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Public-health guidance recognises social and environmental context.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Adolescent wellbeing involves sleep, activity, coping skills and supportive environments; adult advice is not interchangeable.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Age-specific public-health guidance, not a youth treatment programme.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Teen reading pathway ages 13–17; seek trusted adult/professional support.

claims.scientificClaim: Exercise interventions can improve some subjective and objective sleep outcomes.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Original abstract assessed; heterogeneous interventions/measures and no best-exercise claim.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: Sleep extension affected short-term energy intake in a selected sample of habitual short sleepers.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Randomised trial supports this short-term outcome; wider generalisation low certainty.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Younger adults with overweight and habitual short sleep; short intervention.

claims.scientificClaim: Supported combined diet-and-activity programmes can delay diabetes in selected high-risk adults; this does not validate an app score or prove synergy.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Cochrane moderate certainty for incidence; older evidence and high-risk population.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Mostly adults with impaired glucose tolerance; not a general treatment recommendation.

claims.scientificClaim: Capability, opportunity and motivation provide a framework for understanding behaviour.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: No direct contradiction identified in the assessed sources; search was not exhaustive.
claims.certaintyRationale: Framework evidence is not proof of Healthcrest efficacy.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.

claims.scientificClaim: The Explorer illustrates selected settings; its colours, thresholds and shapes are not body measurements or a validated combined health score.
claims.contradictoryEvidence: The software omits important dimensions. No combined risk-reduction magnitude may be inferred.
claims.certaintyRationale: No clinical validation for the software model. Guidance citations provide context only, not model validation.
claims.certaintyMethod: Editorial appraisal, not formal independent GRADE
claims.population: Adults; adapt to health, ability and circumstances.
